bridge: Builds on C01 compilation and P03 indexing. Use the same local compiler and disposable files.
teaching:
An array is a contiguous sequence of elements. For char name[4], valid indices are 0 through 3. A C string additionally needs a zero byte marking its end. Three visible characters plus the terminator fill four bytes; the terminator is data occupying a real position.

An array does not carry a universal runtime bounds check. A function receiving a pointer generally needs a separate capacity contract. Reading beyond the last element is a defect even when it does not immediately crash. Distinguish input byte count, allocated capacity and visible character count, especially when using UTF-8.

A safe interface checks available capacity before copying and reports failure explicitly. Truncation is not always acceptable: truncating an identifier could select a different account or resource. Decide whether to reject, truncate or resize based on the application's meaning. Do not use a successful print as proof that the buffer was large enough.
explanation: The comparison rejects a source whose visible byte length leaves no room for the terminator. Copying strlen+1 includes the terminator. This small example assumes src is already a valid terminated string; strlen itself cannot safely validate an arbitrary unterminated buffer.
exercise: Run with src="cat", then src="cats", then src="". Predict output and exit status before each run. Draw all occupied indices for each accepted input.
solution: cat prints and returns 0. cats is rejected with status 1 and no copy. Empty input stores only a zero byte and prints an empty line. No case should read or write beyond dst[3].
challenge: A destination has capacity 6 bytes. Decide whether ASCII inputs "hello", "planet" and "" fit as terminated strings. Explain why a five-character Unicode string may still fail this byte-capacity check.
challenge_solution: hello fits exactly with its terminator; planet needs7 bytes and is rejected; empty needs1. UTF-8 characters can occupy multiple bytes, so visible character count does not establish byte length.
